prompt: We want to run an A/B test on our pricing page headline. How many visitors do we need and how long should we run it?
must_include: Reaches the feasibility-gate flagship rather than the readout/interpretation reference — this is a before-you-run question, not an after-the-fact one

prompt: We're a small self-serve SaaS with about 3,000 signups a month. Can we A/B test a new onboarding flow, and if so how?
must_include: surface-selfserve.md is still read even though overlay-small-sample.md is additive on top of it, never a replacement for the base surface
Reaches activation-and-onboarding.md for the CUPED-fails-for-new-users content rather than treating overlay-small-sample.md alone as sufficient

prompt: Our agent watches the experiment dashboard and wants to auto-stop the test the moment it crosses significance. Is that okay?
must_include: States the agent may not stop or ship on an interim peek without a peek-safe method configured from the start

prompt: We've been checking our test's dashboard every day and it just crossed p<0.05. Can we ship the winner?
must_include: Frames the answer around how many times the dashboard was checked (K), not a bare peeking warning

prompt: Our signup-to-paid funnel has a huge drop at step 3. Which retention definition should I use to check if it's actually a cohort problem?
must_include: Names at least one of the three retention definitions (N-day, rolling, survival) and which question it answers

prompt: We ranked 20 growth ideas with an ICE score. Is that a sound way to decide what to build next?
must_include: Treats ICE skeptically as throughput tooling rather than as evidence a ranked idea will actually work

prompt: We want to build a win-back campaign for lapsed users and are considering a streak feature to boost retention. Good ideas?
must_include: Points to monetization-and-pricing-experiments.md's ethics section for habit-design ethics rather than re-teaching dark-patterns/habit ethics in this reference

prompt: We want to build a referral program. How do we know whether it'll actually compound growth over time?
must_include: Applies loop math (K-factor, cycle time, or compounding arithmetic) rather than treating 'we have a referral program' as sufficient

prompt: We want to test a new pricing page using a Van Westendorp survey. Good approach?
must_include: States the stated-preference critique of Van Westendorp alongside its provenance, not just its procedure

prompt: Is a 40% 'very disappointed' Sean Ellis score good for our PLG product?
must_include: Carries Sean Ellis's own generalizability caveat on the 40% test alongside the figure, not the figure alone

prompt: We rolled out a price change to every customer at once instead of running an A/B test. How do we know if it worked?
must_include: Reaches for a precondition checklist rather than inventing a numeric sample-size floor for a quasi-experimental method

prompt: We're a B2B SaaS where every deal goes through a sales rep demo before signup. How should we think about testing here?
must_include: Does not default to the self-serve surface once a human-gated sales conversation is stated explicitly

prompt: We run IAP subscriptions in our iOS app and want to test a paywall design. What should I know about the data?
must_include: Frames the RevenueCat-layer dataset as high-N but low-external-validity, requiring vendor and edition-year on every figure

prompt: We're a two-sided marketplace and worried a supply-side test will bias results because sellers interact with each other. What do we do?
must_include: Diagnoses the interference mechanism first rather than defaulting to a specific fix like switchbacks

prompt: Explain exactly how the chi-square test for sample ratio mismatch works, and walk me through CUPED's variance-reduction formula step by step.
must_include: Names data's experiment-measurement-foundations.md by name as the owner of SRM and CUPED mechanics rather than re-deriving either formula here

prompt: Which paid channel should we put more budget behind to get more signups into the top of our funnel?
must_include: Declines to make a channel or spend allocation decision and routes it to marketing
Offers to design or size an experiment testing a channel hypothesis marketing has already proposed, rather than originating the channel choice itself

prompt: We want a permanent error-rate threshold that pages on-call whenever a live production feature regresses. How should we design that?
must_include: States the standing-threshold-on-a-live-system vs. single-tested-change distinction and routes the standing threshold to operate
Does not treat a permanent production alert threshold as an experiment design question

prompt: What should our three pricing tiers be, and what should each one cost?
must_include: Declines to set tier structure or price points and routes that decision to product
Offers to design the experiment testing a tier or price product has already chosen, not to choose it

prompt: Lay out the sections of our new pricing-page hero for the test variant we're about to run.
must_include: Declines page composition and layout and routes it to design
States that growth defines and evaluates the variant while design composes it, rather than proposing a section order itself

prompt: We're a tiny SaaS doing about 800 signups a month total, and want to test a new activation email. Can we run this as a real test?
must_include: Runs the feasibility gate first and names the Ambition Tax or the three levers rather than a bare 'not enough traffic' refusal
Reaches activation-and-onboarding.md for the CUPED-fails-for-new-users constraint on top of the small-sample redirect, not overlay-small-sample.md alone

prompt: We're a B2B SaaS selling annual contracts through a sales team. Is our account retention actually improving?
must_include: States the unit of analysis is the account, not the user, and reads retention as logo retention and gross/net revenue retention rather than an N-day, rolling, or survival window
Does not invent an NRR benchmark figure

prompt: We're a two-sided marketplace building a referral program between sellers and want to test whether it actually compounds growth.
must_include: Names the referral test as a SUTVA/interference violation (inviter leaks treatment into control) before sizing it as a standard user-level test
Diagnoses the marketplace interference mechanism rather than defaulting to switchback randomization by name

prompt: Someone found a case study where a red button beat a blue button and wants us to just ship the same change on our signup page. Good idea?
must_include: Applies the external-validity lesson: a color-pattern win on someone else's page is not evidence it transfers to this one

prompt: Our team keeps saying 'build loops, not funnels' in planning meetings. What does that actually mean, and is it settled fact?
must_include: Names the loops-vs-funnels lineage and notes the named voices are a tight, mutually-amplifying cluster rather than independent convergence

prompt: We just read out a pricing experiment. Who do we hand the result to, and what's still growth's job versus someone else's?
must_include: Names product as the owner of the pricing tiers/hypothesis and states growth hands back the readout rather than setting the tier itself
